subject: Clarify per-call min charge vs aggregated long-context billing for ACME pilot
messages:
From: Susan Carter <susan.carter@acmehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Thu, 05 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot pricing question — rounding on long transcripts

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team liked the latency and the KV reuse. Procurement asked for a sample invoice and one clarification before we start the pilot: how do you handle billing for very long single requests (we'll be sending chunked transcriptions ~35k tokens in one session)?

Specifically:
- If a single transcript is 35k tokens, do you apply a per-request minimum first and then add tokens, or do you aggregate across the session for rounding?
- Do you round up to a billing quantum (e.g., nearest 100 tokens) per request, or is there a daily aggregation that could reduce rounding inefficiency?

We need an example line-item we can include in the PO. I attached the statement template procurement uses — would appreciate a sample invoice row for a 35k-token request and then for a day with 120 such requests.

Thanks,
Susan
Susan Carter
Head of Procurement, ACME Health
Attachments: sample_statement.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Susan Carter <susan.carter@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Jun 2025 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing question — rounding on long transcripts

Hi Susan — great question, thanks for the clear asks. Short answer below, plus two worked examples. Attaching the quick pricing calc (spreadsheet) for the PO team.

How we bill (summary):
- Base unit: 1 token.
- Billing quantum: for efficiency across models we round usage up to the nearest 8-token block when the request is smaller than one model stride, but for long single-request contexts (>8k tokens) we switch to an aggregation path that charges exact token counts with a per-request floor that can be waived for pilots.
- Per-request floor: default is 64 tokens (applies to tiny calls only); it does NOT meaningfully affect >1k token calls.
- Long-context handling: for single requests >8k tokens we bill actual tokens consumed (input + output) without the 8-token block rounding; however we apply a per-call minimum billing cap only if the customer chooses the "per-call guaranteed latency tier".

Worked example A — single 35,000-token transcript (no output tokens for simplicity):
- Rule: single large request (>8k) billed on exact token count.
- Billed tokens = 35,000
- If using quantized model variant there may be a small (2–3%) effective reduction; show both in the spreadsheet.

Worked example B — daily aggregate of 120 calls at ~35k tokens each:
- Each call billed individually on exact token counts by default (no per-day auto-aggregation).
- Total billed tokens = 120 * 35,000 = 4,200,000 tokens.
- If you want to reduce rounding inefficiency for many small calls we can enable daily aggregation (experimental) that consolidates sub-8k calls into a single-day bucket to reduce block rounding; not applicable to these large calls.

Pilot concession: to simplify PO/invoicing we can provide a one-time rounding credit equal to 1% of total billed tokens for the pilot month (applied as a line-item credit) and temporarily waive the per-call floor. This is negotiable.

I'll let Vanessa confirm commercial terms (credits, commitments) and Marissa can help produce the sample invoice row for your template. Spreadsheet attached.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: pricing-math.xlsx

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Susan Carter <susan.carter@acmehealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Jun 2025 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing question — rounding on long transcripts

Thanks Karthik / Susan — quick commercial note from our side. We appreciate the signal volume here and can make two changes for the pilot to keep the invoice clean for procurement:

1) Pilot rounding credit: we will apply a one-time 1% token credit for the pilot month (applied as a positive line on the invoice). That covers minor model quantization variance and any per-request round-up inefficiency.

2) Per-call floor waiver: we will waive the 64-token floor for any request over 1,000 tokens for the pilot. Effectively, for your 35k transcripts we will bill exact tokens.

3) Optional aggregation feature: if you prefer, we can enable a daily aggregation mode for medium calls (500–8,000 tokens) that collapses those into a single daily bucket per account to remove block rounding. Note: aggregation introduces a 24-hour reporting lag and is not applied to >8k calls.

4) Example invoice rows (sample numbers):
- Single 35,000-token call (no output): Billed tokens = 35,000; unit price = $0.0008/token => line = $28.00
- 120 calls at 35,000 tokens each: Billed tokens = 4,200,000; pre-credit = $3,360.00; pilot credit (1%) = -$33.60; net = $3,326.40

5) PO and cadence: we can accept monthly invoices. If you need Net-45 we can do that with a small administration fee (0.25% of invoice).

Marissa, can you prepare a sample invoice row that fits Susan's attached template and include the credit line and payment terms (Net-30/Net-45 options)? Karthik, please confirm deal ID so accounting maps correctly.

Thanks — Vanessa
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Susan Carter <susan.carter@acmehealth.com>
